questions.q: What generates the standard dbt project folder structure shown in this lesson?
options: dbt init (or dbt Cloud's project setup) — the same skeleton either way
A manual folder-by-folder setup with no standard structure
It's randomly different for every warehouse
Only dbt Cloud can generate a project structure
questions.explain: Whether via dbt init (dbt Core) or dbt Cloud's setup, the generated project skeleton is the same.

questions.q: Where do a dbt project's transformation SQL files live?
options: models/
tests/
data/
packages.yml
questions.explain: models/ is where the .sql transformation files live — the bulk of the work in a dbt project.

questions.q: What does the `profile:` line inside dbt_project.yml actually do?
options: Names a connection profile by reference — the real credentials live outside the project, not in this file
Stores the warehouse username and password directly
Nothing — it's an optional, unused field
It sets the dbt Cloud subscription tier
questions.explain: profile: only names a profile; the actual connection details are configured separately (covered in the next lesson), never checked into the project.

questions.q: What is a 'seed' in a dbt project, and where does it live?
options: A small static .csv file dbt loads as a table, stored under the data/ (or seeds/) folder
A compiled SQL file generated automatically in target/
A macro that seeds random test data into production
A YAML file that defines warehouse credentials
questions.explain: Seeds are small static CSV files dbt can load directly as tables, kept in the data/ or seeds/ folder.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say the folder split (models/, macros/, tests/, data/) is not arbitrary?
options: It lets dbt and anyone skimming the file tree know exactly what kind of file something is, without opening it
It's required by the SQL language itself
Warehouses enforce this folder structure at the database level
It has no real purpose — it's just convention with no benefit
questions.explain: The consistent folder split makes a project's contents predictable at a glance — a .sql file under tests/ is always an assertion, one under models/ is always a transformation step.
